items.title: Temesgen Weldemihret, Tesfamichael Ymesghen, and Haben Tesfay, Erican Foundation
notes:
T. Weldemihret, T. Ymesghen, and H. Tesfay appeared before Council to express their concerns with transnational repression from the Eritrean government. They provided an overview of the actions of the government and their supporters in Canada, and highlighted issues with ongoing intimidation of Eritrean Canadians.

In response to a question from Council, they stated that they are victims of ongoing intimidation from the Eritrean government. They requested the opportunity to work with Council and the Regional police to come to a solution.

items.title: Muhammad Aftab Nazir, Kitchener
notes: M. Nazir not appear when called.

items.title: Sean Campbell, Union Co-operative
notes: S. Campbell appeared before Council in support of the preservation of existing affordable housing. He encouraged the Region to look at options for preserving affordable housing and stressed that preserving affordable units is more affordable than building new ones.

items.title: Aaron Stauch, Kitchener
notes: A. Stauch appeared in support of the Property Tax Exemption Program for Affordable Housing. He stressed that we can’t build our way out of the affordable housing crisis and noted that the by-law will support the preservation of much needed affordable housing.

items.title: Kae Elgie, Waterloo
notes: K. Elgie noted that a slide deck was provided that is appended to the original minutes and contains a link to a film that speaks to housing as a human right. She stressed the need for affordable housing that should cost less than 30% of a household’s income, and encouraged Council to support the property tax exemption.

items.title: Kay Valley, HomeBAnx
notes:
K. Valley appeared on behalf of HomeBAnx, noting that they are working to help Black women and members of the 2SLGBTQ+ community to get into home ownership. She stressed that systemic racism has negatively impacted them as business owners and that there is a needed for targeted financial confidence programs. She shared that they are working with financial institutions to structure the program and that they have met with Regional staff and are receiving support. 

In response to a question from Council, Peter Sweeney, Commissioner, Community Services stated that staff can provide information on on equity and how it fits into the plan to end chronic homelessness.

items.title: Alfred Lowrick, Wilmot
notes:
A. Lowrick appeared on behalf of land owners in Wilmot Township that have been informed that their land will be expropriated. He stated that the group was approached by a consultant to purchase their properties with a short deadline. He expressed concerns that prime agricultural land would be taken and stressed that this is contrary to many of the Region’s stated environmental and planning goals. He encouraged the Region to look elsewhere for the land. 

Regional Chair K. Redman noted that due to the confidential nature Council cannot comment but encouraged A. Lowrick to speak with Matthew Chandy, Director, Innovation & Economic Development.

items.title: Vaughn Bender, Schlegel Urban Developments
notes:
V. Bender appeared before Council with respect to report EES-WAS-24-001, Proposed Bill 162 (Get it Done Act) and Drinking Water Supply Implications for Waterloo Region, noting that a portion of the lands referred to in the report belong to Schlegel Urban Developments. He circulated a document that is appended to the original minutes. V. Bender stated that the City of Kitchener has supported having these lands included in City of Kitchener. He stressed that these lands are appropriate for development under the Region’s policies and that there is capacity in the existing infrastructure. He noted that they have the potential to increase the ground water recharge and will not result in increased chloride concentration. He requested that the Region support the City of Kitchener moving forward with these lands.

Responding to questions, V. Bender stated that they appreciate the importance of ground water recharge and have done a significant amount of work monitoring the water in the area and that infiltration targets can be met and exceeded. He further noted that their lands are not part of the protected countryside line and that agriculture poses a greater risk to groundwater than residential.

items.title: Richard Murphy, Steve Harris, and Andrew Betts, GHD
notes:
R. Murphy noted that the Regional Recharge Area is not consistent with the source water protection plan. He stressed that residential development is not a prescribed threat under the Act. He further noted that if the BSF2 lands are analyzed with the same criteria as the Southwest Kitchener Policy Area, they should be excluded from the Regional Recharge Area.

In response to a question from Council, R. Murphy and A. Betts explained that they have conducted studies to design facilities that capture water and facilitate it getting into the ground. They noted that they have found the areas on the land that have the highest infiltration and will protect those areas and encourage further infiltration.

Responding to questions, V. Bender stated that Regional staff have acknowledged that residential development can safely happen on this land, but that there is a policy decision why the development can go ahead. He questioned whether the Regional policy requirements should be different than in other places in the province.

items.title: Brad Trussler, Mattamy Homes
notes: B. Trussler appeared on behalf of Mattamy Homes noting that their lands are also outlined in report EES-WAS-24-001, Proposed Bill 162 (Get it Done Act) and Drinking Water Supply Implications for Waterloo Region. He explained that the lands are designated as part of the urban boundary and highlighted work that they have done on another site to clean up soil and ensure long term clean water recharge. He stressed that these lands will benefit the Region and requested that the Region support the City of Kitchener’s position on the lands.

items.title: Planning and Works Committee Summary - March 5, 2024
Community and Health Services Committee Summary - March 5, 2024
Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health, informed Council that there have been no locally reported cases of measles but with increased travel over March break, she expects that to change in the near future. She provided an overview of the recommended vaccination schedule for measles. Dr. H. Wang stated that with one week remaining before school suspensions, there are still 6,000 student records remain. She provided an overview of the steps that  parents can take to avoid suspension.

In response to a question from Council, Dr. H. Wang stated that a number of viruses have reappeared and are circulating at a rate prior to the pandemic. Scarlet Fever and Group A Strep are some of those, whereas measles had very few cases in Canada prior to the pandemic but vaccination rates have waned over the pandemic.

Received for information.

items.title: Other Matters Under Committee Of The Whole
EES-WAS-24-001, Proposed Bill 162 (Get it Done Act) and Drinking Water Supply Implications for Waterloo Region
notes:
Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering and Environmental Services introduced the report noting that it outlines staff’s comments on Bill 162, to be submitted to the province. She noted that 75% of the Region’s water comes from aquifers in the ground and 45% comes from the Waterloo moraine. She stressed that this moraine is critical to the Region’s growth, which is why it was protected by the Regional Recharge Area. She noted that increased development results in increased salt levels in the ground water and that if the Bill is passed as is, it will limit the number of homes built in the Region. 

In response to a question from Council, Rod Regier, Commissioner, Planning, Development, and Legislative Services stated that it is not necessary to build in the Regional Recharge Area in order to meet housing targets. 

Responding to questions, J. Rose stated that the window for commenting on the Bill was opened 30 days ago. She explained that the area municipalities are able to provide their own comments to the province and noted that the Clean Water Act is the purview of the Region and the area municipalities were not consulted on the comments. She further explained that staff have worked with the delegations to incorporate their data into the tier 3 water model. Staff are concerned that the infrastructure that the delegations are proposing will be privately owned and will not be maintained by a municipality. She stressed the importance of maintaining a multi-barrier approach to ensure that ground water is protected in the Region of Waterloo.

B. Vrbanovic brought forward a motion to direct staff to not submit the report to the Environmental Registry of Ontario. Council discussed and debated the motion. 

The report was received for information.

motions.item_title: Community and Health Services Committee Summary - March 5, 2024
motions.text: That the following recommendations from the Community and Health Services Committee be approved: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve an increase of $1,542,836 to the 2024 Homelessness and Supportive Housing Operating Budget expenditure and federal subsidy with no net property tax levy impact as outlined in report COR-CFN-24-001 dated March 5, 2024. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action for preserving existing affordable housing in the private market and facilitating the transition of private market rentals into long-term affordable housing through acquisition as outlined in CSD-HOU-24-003, dated March 5, 2024: Direct staff to explore the creation of a Multi-Unit Rental Acquisition Program to preserve existing affordable housing in the private market and facilitate the transition of private market rentals into long-term affordable housing; and For staff to bring forward any recommendations to the Regional Council for consideration; Direct staff to work with the area municipalities to explore the creation of right of first refusal policy and identification of affordable housing at risk of loss; and Direct staff to work with area municipalities to assemble a Waterloo Region Housing Needs Assessment to inform a targeted affordable housing acquisition strategy. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to rental housing protections and tenant displacement as outlined in CSD-HOU-24-003, dated March 5, 2024: Direct staff to work with the area municipalities to explore the creation of renovation, conversion, and demolition rental housing protection policies; Direct staff to engage with service providers who support tenants at risk of or are currently experiencing displacement to: Identify gaps in support of displaced tenants and for tenants at risk of experiencing eviction caused by renovation, demolition, or conversion; Develop potential solutions to fill gaps; and Bring forward gaps and potential solutions to the Regional Council for consideration. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to advocating for the preservation of existing affordable housing as outlined in CSD-HOU-24-003, dated March 5, 2024: Request that the Government of Canada and the Government of Ontario establish acquisition programs that would support the acquisitions and renovations/conversions for all types of private market residential properties and other properties, to create new permanent affordable and supportive homes. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the creation of a Property Tax Exemption Program for Affordable Housing as set out in report CSD-HOU-24-004 dated March 5, 2024: Repeal By-law Number 02-035, attached as Appendix “A”, and replace with By-Law Number 24-***, attached as Appendix “B” for the purposes of updating the by-law to allow Council to exempt regional and education property taxes for municipal housing facilities and also for general house-keeping amendments, which has been prepared in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor; Approve the Property Tax Exemption for Affordable Housing Program (“Program”) and guidelines for applications made to the Region for properties eligible for the Program attached as Appendix “C”; Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services to negotiate and execute on behalf of the Region, agreements with housing providers for the Program, to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor; Direct staff to: Develop an application process with intake occurring in Q2 of 2024 for the 2025 taxation year; Review the uptake and application of the Program to determine property tax impacts due to class shifts, communicating these in advance of 2025 budget process; Direct staff to work with interested area municipalities within Waterloo Region to exempt the lower tier portion of property taxes for eligible properties under the Program; and Advocate to the Government of Ontario to amend eligibility for the Ontario Trillium Benefit to allow Ontario residents living in housing deemed affordable by the municipality where the resident resides, to access property tax credits through the Ontario Trillium Benefit, irrespective of property tax exemption.
motions.text_html:
That the following recommendations from the Community and Health Services Committee be approved:

  1. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo approve an increase of $1,542,836 to the 2024 Homelessness and Supportive Housing Operating Budget expenditure and federal subsidy with no net property tax levy impact as outlined in report COR-CFN-24-001 dated March 5, 2024.
  2. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action for preserving existing affordable housing in the private market and facilitating the transition of private market rentals into long-term affordable housing through acquisition as outlined in CSD-HOU-24-003, dated March 5, 2024:
    1. Direct staff to explore the creation of a Multi-Unit Rental Acquisition Program to preserve existing affordable housing in the private market and facilitate the transition of private market rentals into long-term affordable housing; and
      1. For staff to bring forward any recommendations to the Regional Council for consideration;
    2. Direct staff to work with the area municipalities to explore the creation of right of first refusal policy and identification of affordable housing at risk of loss; and
    3. Direct staff to work with area municipalities to assemble a Waterloo Region Housing Needs Assessment to inform a targeted affordable housing acquisition strategy.
  3. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to rental housing protections and tenant displacement as outlined in CSD-HOU-24-003, dated March 5, 2024:
    1. Direct staff to work with the area municipalities to explore the creation of renovation, conversion, and demolition rental housing protection policies;
    2. Direct staff to engage with service providers who support tenants at risk of or are currently experiencing displacement to:
      1. Identify gaps in support of displaced tenants and for tenants at risk of experiencing eviction caused by renovation, demolition, or conversion;
      2. Develop potential solutions to fill gaps; and
      3. Bring forward gaps and potential solutions to the Regional Council for consideration.
  4. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to advocating for the preservation of existing affordable housing as outlined in CSD-HOU-24-003, dated March 5, 2024:
    1. Request that the Government of Canada and the Government of Ontario establish acquisition programs that would support the acquisitions and renovations/conversions for all types of private market residential properties and other properties, to create new permanent affordable and supportive homes.
  5. That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the creation of a Property Tax Exemption Program for Affordable Housing as set out in report CSD-HOU-24-004 dated March 5, 2024:
    1. Repeal By-law Number 02-035, attached as Appendix “A”, and replace with By-Law Number 24-***, attached as Appendix “B” for the purposes of updating the by-law to allow Council to exempt regional and education property taxes for municipal housing facilities and also for general house-keeping amendments, which has been prepared in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor;
    2. Approve the Property Tax Exemption for Affordable Housing Program (“Program”) and guidelines for applications made to the Region for properties eligible for the Program attached as Appendix “C”;
    3. Authorize the Commissioner of Community Services to negotiate and execute on behalf of the Region, agreements with housing providers for the Program, to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor;
    4. Direct staff to:
      1. Develop an application process with intake occurring in Q2 of 2024 for the 2025 taxation year;
      2. Review the uptake and application of the Program to determine property tax impacts due to class shifts, communicating these in advance of 2025 budget process;
    5. Direct staff to work with interested area municipalities within Waterloo Region to exempt the lower tier portion of property taxes for eligible properties under the Program; and
    6. Advocate to the Government of Ontario to amend eligibility for the Ontario Trillium Benefit to allow Ontario residents living in housing deemed affordable by the municipality where the resident resides, to access property tax credits through the Ontario Trillium Benefit, irrespective of property tax exemption.

motions.item_title: Councillor D. Craig Notice of Motion
motions.text: Be it further resolved that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo calls on the Ontario Government to: immediately re-open the Consumption and Treatment Site (CTS) process; eliminate the cap of 21 sites province-wide; eliminate the ban on inhalation accommodations; and revise the CTS process to reduce the bureaucratic burden for applicants and expedite the establishment of safe consumption sites. And that this request be sent to the Premier of Ontario and the ministers for Health, Mental Health and Addictions and Finance as well as the area members of provincial parliament in the Region of Waterloo.
motions.text_html:
Be it further resolved that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo calls on the Ontario Government to:

  1.  immediately re-open the Consumption and Treatment Site (CTS) process;
  2. eliminate the cap of 21 sites province-wide;
  3. eliminate the ban on inhalation accommodations; and
  4. revise the CTS process to reduce the bureaucratic burden for applicants and expedite the establishment of safe consumption sites.

And that this request be sent to the Premier of Ontario and the ministers for Health, Mental Health and Addictions and Finance as well as the area members of provincial parliament in the Region of Waterloo.

motions.item_title: Councillor D. Craig Notice of Motion
motions.text: Whereas, there has been a reported 720 overdose deaths in the Region of Waterloo since 2018, And whereas, a Region of Waterloo Feasibility Study (February 2018) found that there were an estimated 4000 users in the Region with approximately 2000 users injecting drugs daily, And whereas, 79% of people surveyed reported injecting drugs alone, increasing the risk of fatal overdoses, And whereas, inhalation is preferred among people without stable housing in Waterloo Region and is suspected in approximately half the deaths in Ontario, And whereas, a major conclusion of the Feasibility Report was that the stated figures were an underestimation, Therefore, be it resolved, that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct Public Health staff to provide a report, by the end of 2024 Q2, to increase awareness and understanding of the scope of the drug overdose and addictions issues in the Region of Waterloo And that this report include: data on the current situation (e.g. how many are using, what are they using, where are they using); an overview of Public Health and Community Services activities in response; and an overview of the current federal, provincial and local initiatives to address problematic substance abuse.
motions.text_html:
Whereas, there has been a reported 720 overdose deaths in the Region of Waterloo since 2018, 

And whereas, a Region of Waterloo Feasibility Study (February 2018) found that there were an estimated 4000 users in the Region with approximately 2000 users injecting drugs daily, 

And whereas, 79% of people surveyed reported injecting drugs alone, increasing the risk of fatal overdoses,

And whereas, inhalation is preferred among people without stable housing in Waterloo Region and is suspected in approximately half the deaths in Ontario,

And whereas, a major conclusion of the Feasibility Report was that the stated figures were an underestimation,

Therefore, be it resolved, that the Regional Municipality of Waterloo direct Public Health staff to provide a report, by the end of 2024 Q2, to increase awareness and understanding of the scope of the drug overdose and addictions issues in the Region of Waterloo 

And that this report include:

  1. data on the current situation (e.g. how many are using, what are they using, where are they using);
  2. an overview of Public Health and Community Services activities in response; and
  3. an overview of the current federal, provincial and local initiatives to address problematic substance abuse.
